title: Generate exhaustive configuration setting inventory and doc coverage check
description:
Problem: Data/Pages/guides/configuration-reference.md is useful as an operator map, but it groups many settings instead of listing every editable key. A 2026-05-25 scan of AdminSettingsService found 161 editable setting descriptors, while the guide documents many of them as groups such as Auth:*, Chat:*, Logging:*, Telemetry:*, and MaintenanceAgent:*. That is readable, but agents looking for an exact setting key need a machine-checkable inventory.

Desired outcome: provide an exhaustive, generated or validated configuration-key inventory that complements the human guide and fails when editable settings drift without docs.

Scope:
- In scope: extract editable setting descriptors from AdminSettingsService or a shared descriptor source, emit a grouped key inventory with label/category/help/sensitivity metadata, and add a lightweight validation that flags undocumented new keys or intentionally grouped keys.
- Out of scope: redesigning the admin settings UI or changing setting semantics.

Acceptance criteria:
- Every editable setting key has a discoverable docs entry or an explicit grouped-coverage marker.
- The generated inventory is linked from configuration-reference.md and useful to agents configuring MemorySmith.
- Sensitive/write-only settings are clearly marked without exposing values.
- A local validation command reports drift when a new EditableSettingDescriptor is added without coverage.

Validation:
- Run the new configuration docs coverage check if implemented.
- Run ./Scripts/Test-PageLinks.ps1 and ./Scripts/Test-PagePathLiterals.ps1 after docs updates.
- Run ./Scripts/Test-TaskRecords.ps1 after task metadata changes.

comments.author: AgentSmith
comments.body: Created during 2026-05-25 deepdive audit. Evidence: descriptor extraction from MemorySmith.App/Services/AdminSettingsService.cs found 161 editable keys; Data/Pages/guides/configuration-reference.md documents the active configuration as grouped operator guidance rather than a complete per-key inventory. The page now states that limitation explicitly.
